title: Introduce length-aware inflight reservation to address short-flow starvation and long-context tail spikes
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Multiple customers have reported recurring high p50->p95 latency regressions driven by long-context requests dominating continuous-batcher admission and causing small, latency-sensitive flows to be starved. The symptom set: elevated short-request latency, KV cache eviction churn, and persistent long-context backlog in the batcher queues across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This ticket implements a 'length-aware inflight reservation' mechanism: the scheduler will reserve a small fraction of inflight slots and admission capacity for short-context requests (<= 512 tokens) while adapting reservation size based on observed mix and backlog to avoid throughput loss for long-context workloads.
repro_steps: Deploy continuous-batcher with default admission settings in a staging cluster
Generate mixed workload: 70% long-context (2k-8k tokens) steady stream, 30% short-context (<=256 tokens) bursty traffic from an emulated tenant
Observe short-request p95 increase and KV cache eviction spikes during long-context waves
Capture scheduler metrics: admission_count_by_length, inflight_reserved_slots, queue_depth_by_length
Reproduce across hosted and a private VPC staging instance to confirm cross-deployment behavior
investigation_notes: Telemetry showed that long-context requests monopolize admission windows because their effective 'token-time' holds capacity for many ticks. Prefetch/kv-population for long contexts causes eviction of short-flow KV segments, leading to repeated cache misses and amplification of their latency. Past mitigations (prefetch quarantine, admission smoothing) reduced but did not eliminate regressions under mixed waves. Key observation: when short requests are starved, they re-enter the queue and get grouped into later, larger mixed batches that further increase their latency (backlog amplification).
proposed_fix: Implement a lightweight inflight reservation in the admission controller: reserve an adaptive percentage (default 8%) of inflight slots for requests with estimated length <= 512 tokens. Reservation is time-bound (sliding hold window) and decays when underutilized. The admission decision is length-aware: short requests may be admitted preferentially into reserved slots even if backlog contains long requests. Integrate with KV cache hysteresis to avoid thrashing: pinned KV segments for recently serviced short flows get an eviction grace window tied to the reservation usage metric.
implementation_notes:
- Add admission_reservation config with parameters: base_percent, max_percent, hold_ms, decay_factor.
- Admission path change should be limited to fast checks (length bucket, reservation counter) to avoid adding latency.
- Update telemetry: admission.reservation.allocated, used, short_flow_block_count, kv.eviction_by_length.
- Add unit tests for corner cases (reservation full, sustained short-only traffic, long-only traffic).
- Add canary flag to enable per-cluster and per-tenant gating.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag; deploy to canary hosts in staging. 2) Run mixed workload soak (48h) with chaos injection (tenant microbursts). 3) Roll to 5% of production hosts for hosted customers and to dedicated staging tenants for enterprise customers. 4) Monitor key signals for 24-72h: short_request_p95, overall throughput, kv_eviction_rate. 5) Gradually increase to 100% if no regression; provide immediate rollback plan to toggle flag per-host.
acceptance_criteria:
- short_request_p95 decreases by >=40% under mixed workloads without increasing overall tail latency beyond 10% of baseline.
- KV eviction rate attributable to short-flow churn reduces by >=30% in controlled tests.
- No throughput regression >3% in steady long-context-only workload.
- Canary rollout shows stable metrics for 72 hours and no customer escalations.
- Unit and integration tests cover admission edge cases and race conditions.
